issues.description: Compiled script content is inlined into the compile RPC response instead of being fetched on demand via a path-based download endpoint.
issues.detail: The compile RPC complects two concerns: where the artifact lives (path) and what it contains (bytes). Every compile response now reads the full file into memory, JSON-encodes it, ships it over RPC, holds it in React state, and re-encodes it as a Blob — with no size bound. A dedicated download endpoint keyed by path would decouple these and avoid unbounded payloads.

issues.description: open(script_path) lacks explicit encoding and any stated precondition tying the file to compile_pipeline's postcondition.
issues.detail: The read relies on the platform-default encoding rather than asserting UTF-8 as an invariant of compiled-script output. There is also no stated contract that compile_pipeline guarantees the file exists and is readable, and no separation between compilation failure and serialization failure. State the contract and pass encoding='utf-8'.

issues.description: Object URL and DOM anchor are not revoked on the exception path; lifecycle is implicit.
issues.detail: createObjectURL allocates a resource whose revoke happens inline after click(). If click() throws, or the component unmounts mid-flight, the Blob URL and orphan anchor leak. Wrap in try/finally (or tie lifecycle to a useEffect cleanup) so the cleanup invariant holds unconditionally.

issues.description: Filename derivation via split('/').pop() with a fabricated fallback hides path-shape and naming bugs.
issues.detail: split('/').pop() assumes POSIX separators (breaks on Windows-hosted notebook servers) and || 'pipeline.kale.py' silently substitutes a fabricated name. Either compiledPath is guaranteed non-empty and forward-slash-delimited at the boundary (then the fallback is dead) or it is not (then users get a misnamed file). Reason about which case holds.

issues.description: GetAppIcon is used as an interactive control without button semantics or keyboard support.
issues.detail: An onClick on a bare SVG icon is not keyboard-reachable and exposes no accessible role. Wrap in a <button> or IconButton with aria-label so focus, activation, and assistive-tech announcements work. Use the correct primitive rather than smuggling activation through an icon.

issues.description: Imperative create-anchor-click-revoke dance lacks both a literate comment and a declarative alternative.
issues.detail: The Blob to object URL to synthetic anchor to click to revoke sequence is six steps of place-oriented DOM mutation expressing one fact: trigger a file save. Either replace with a declarative <a download href={objectUrl}> rendered conditionally, or add a short comment stating the invariants (URL revoked on every exit path, anchor removed even on error).

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the feature works but is structurally over-engineered for what is conceptually a file download. The dominant issue, flagged unanimously, is that the compile RPC inlines the full script content alongside the path — complecting identity with value, with no size bound, no explicit encoding, and no stated precondition tying the read to compile_pipeline's postcondition. The frontend then double-buffers the bytes as a Blob and triggers download through an imperative anchor-click dance that leaks on exceptions, derives filenames with POSIX-only assumptions and a fabricated fallback, and exposes the trigger as a non-semantic icon. The correct shape is a path-based download endpoint with an explicit contract; the current shape should be tightened before it outlives its author.
